correctness.rationale: For a selected vertex, the outside-neighbor count is exactly \(n-t\) if its deleted mate is selected and \(n-t-1\) otherwise, with the symmetric formula on the other shore. This yields sharp support lower bounds \(q=n-k\) for intersecting supports and \(r=q-1\) for disjoint supports. Domination forces at least two selected vertices per shore, which resolves the \(k=n-2\) boundary. The constructions attain every bound, and the support classification gives the stated exact counts. Independent finite replay checks both values and counts.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a canonical one-factor deletion of complete bipartite graphs and are regular, so they directly test the newly introduced capacity invariant against its published biclique baseline and regular-graph bridge. The theorem gives a sharp intermediate-capacity phase transition, complete optimum-set structure, and exact counts; it is not a routine finite increment.
